architectural_question: is the GENERIC owner sufficient as a mechanism for a stricter bound execution layer, or does a structural defect remain in the owner itself?
answer: SUFFICIENT AS A MECHANISM. No structural defect found in the owner. One carry-forward gap (outer route-pass accounting) belongs to the next layer by design, and two honest limitations are recorded.

generic_multi_run_behaviour.observed: with no decoder_invocations ceiling, three sequential METADATA_ONLY runs produced decoder_invocations=3, metadata_reads=3 while path_opens stayed 1
generic_multi_run_behaviour.assessment: NOT a defect. The owner is generic and permits multiple plan runs when the budget does not forbid them; the binding layer supplies MAX 1. This is the separation HQ200 describes, and it is the correct design: baking a ceiling into the generic owner would hard-code warrant policy.
generic_multi_run_behaviour.verified_that_the_cap_actually_bites: supplying decoder_invocations=1 turned the identical second run into a pre-operation refusal with zero account movement (criterion C3/C4)

what_the_owner_provides_to_a_binding_lay: one session -> one broker -> one physical open, preserved across every operation in the entry
a separate, gated decoder_invocations account that a binding layer can cap
an explicit typed operation plan with independent row-data mode and reader encoding
plan-gated header-prefix access (None = never; N = exactly one N-byte read)
mode-exact accounting so chunk reads cannot masquerade as full reads
a LIVE aggregate receipt suitable for a per-source warrant receipt
deterministic idempotent close and a context-manager path
fail-closed refusal before any source operation, with accounts unchanged

carry_forward_gap_belonging_to_the_next_.statement: the session does NOT own or enforce full_route_passes (SRC27 expected 1 / max 1). SourceOperationPlan carries an `outer_account_token` field which is recorded in the receipt but is not an account and has no ceiling.
required_next_layer_work: add a separately typed outer route-pass account with its own pre-operation ceiling
do NOT collapse it into decoder_invocations, full_reads, chunk_reads or reader_invocations
execute at most the admitted outer route-pass count; a second pass requires new authority
carry_forward_gap_belonging_to_the_next_.why: HQ200 already adjudicates this as the next runtime layer's responsibility, and the generic owner correctly declines to hard-code it

honest_limitations_of_the_owner_itself.detail: the owner refuses a second entry WITHIN one session when the cap is 1, but an owner object cannot prevent a different PROCESS or a restarted run from constructing its own first session. A warrant-grade 'exactly one route pass' guarantee therefore also needs an authority-held durable mechanism or an operational control. This is a boundary of object-scoped ownership, not a coding defect.

honest_limitations_of_the_owner_itself.limitation: the session does not retain the first observed source SHA
honest_limitations_of_the_owner_itself.detail: expected_source_sha256 is validated on every run() against the constructor value, but the session does not memoise the first observed digest and refuse a later run whose expected value differs. In the current API the expected value is supplied once at construction, so this is not reachable through run(); it would become reachable if a future binding layer allowed the expectation to be re-supplied per run. ADVISORY hardening only.
the owner can enforce a byte ceiling but cannot invent one; no real-source numeric ceiling is source-free frozen, and synthetic totals are not warrant budgets.

warrant_plan_binding_requirements_for_th: validate a bound source-entry plan against the seven exact operation plans
construct exactly one GovernedSourceSession per bound source entry
bind source-INDEPENDENT policy ceilings (e.g. decoder MAX 1) separately from frozen expected values
preserve unknown or source-dependent numeric fields as issuance-blocking rather than inventing numbers
own the outer route-pass account and enforce its max
